report.summary: PostHog is an open-source product and data platform used by 500,000+ teams, now positioning itself as a "context layer" for products and AI agents. It raised a $75M Series E at a $1.4B valuation in Sept 2025 and is growing through inbound, usage-based, free-tier-led adoption rather than outbound sales. It has 230+ employees, over $50M in revenue and a Growth small team.

we're also going to start working on generating pull requests for you.

Inbound-led sales
Use it without talking to us.

facts.claim: 98% of PostHog's customers use it for free; all paid products are pay-per-use with monthly free tiers.
evidence: All our paid products are pay-per-use with generous monthly free tiers. In fact, 98% of our customers use PostHog for free.

facts.claim: PostHog is hiring (11 open team member slots), is a company of 230+ people, has revenue over $50 million a year, and has dedicated small teams including Growth and Demand Gen.
evidence: Our small teams are looking to add 11 team members.

Our revenue is over $50 million a year

evidence: We have 10+ paid products today, and even if we don't offer it yet, we will eventually.

pain_point.title: Converting a 98% free base into paying, multi-product users
pain_point.rationale: PostHog says 98% of customers use it for free (f6), and all paid products are pay-per-use with free tiers. Growth is inbound-led and self-serve, with no sales needed (f5). So the conversion from free to paid, and from one product to the next, probably depends on in-product onboarding rather than people. As Head of Growth, Alex likely owns this. It is a hypothesis that many free users stall before reaching a paid use case. Onboardly's work on finding and fixing onboarding drop-off, and its trial-to-paid result, could plausibly help.

pain_point.title: Keeping KYC-heavy Connect onboarding fast as it scales

This is a hypothesis, not a confirmed problem.
